title: Expertise and trustworthiness markers for website credibility
statement:
Explicit expertise and trustworthiness markers such as credentials, citations, outside sources, and clear policies can strengthen website credibility, giving teams several substantiated ways to answer the objection 'Why should I believe you?'. (Simson)

Options:
- Expert credentials: named-expert-credentials (fits: expert led, high consideration, professional)
- Outside sources: third-party-source-links (fits: evidence led, research backed, high scrutiny)
- Cited claims: cited-product-claims (fits: technical, evidence led, transparent)
- Clear policies: plain-language-policy-links (fits: transparent, risk reducing, service led)
- Detailed specifications: detailed-product-information (fits: technical, comparison shopping, high involvement)
appliesWhen: Applies to: ecommerce, professional services, health information, expert led products. Audience: adults, general.

source.title: What makes Web sites credible?: a report on a large quantitative study
source.authors: B. J. Fogg; Jonathan Marshall; Othman Laraki; Alex Osipovich; Chris Varma; Nicholas Fang; Jyoti Paul; Akshay Rangnekar; John Shon; Preeti Swani; Marissa Treinen
source.venue: Proceedings of the SIGCHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI 2001), ACM
